metadata.api: FindFirstFileW, WIN32_FIND_DATA.dwReserved0; directory-entry enumeration only, followed by FindClose
metadata.meaning: A local Unix-domain socket filesystem endpoint. This tag is not a symbolic-link/junction target and Microsoft defines no public reparse-data structure for it. Target=null does not establish a broken link. The endpoint path is .port itself; peer PID/listener ownership is not recovered from this metadata.
metadata.method_boundary: Same ordinary tool permissions; small in-process Add-Type helper called only FindFirstFileW and FindClose. Did not open/follow the target, connect a socket, change security, or request elevated access. This was metadata inspection, not fixture/game compilation or execution.

data_query.meaning: The file cannot be accessed by the system.
data_query.outcome: No reparse payload retrieved. Did not retry or elevate this operation. Metadata enumeration was a separate officially documented read-only directory query.
data_query.limit: 1920 is not ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED=5 and by itself does not prove an ACL problem. Rider logs previously showed a matching localized access message but did not expose its numeric Win32 code; do not retroactively label their native return code as measured.

official_findings: Microsoft identifies 0x80000023 as AF_UNIX and says this tag has no defined data structure.

Microsoft documents AF_UNIX pathname bind creating a custom NTFS reparse point, and removal of the old socket file before binding the same path again. This explains why ordinary endpoint cleanup can be part of startup; it does not authorize cleanup now or prove deletion will succeed here.

JetBrains SUPPORT-A-4102 is an official DirectoryLock recovery article; indexed text discusses stuck IDE processes and residual lock/port/token files. Its full body and the matching installed-version DirectoryLock source were not retrievable. Its CannotActivateException/BindException scenario is not established equivalent to this machine's FileSystemException/1920. No unverified recipe is promoted as guaranteed recovery.
conclusion: The concrete failing operation is Rider bootstrap socket/lock cleanup. The artifact is an AF_UNIX endpoint, not an ordinary corrupt empty file or a path redirect. Its presence after the first run and the user's manual close are temporally related only; no evidence assigns fault to the user. Windows access error root cause, exact effect of startup context and whether ordinary deletion would work remain unknown.
conditional_recovery_plan_not_executed: Preserve current logs, tag, timestamps and failed receipts. Do not copy a socket node as if it were ordinary backup data.

Before any change, freshly verify that no Rider instance/backends use the relevant installation/profile, and recheck this exact path's AF_UNIX tag and recorded identity. Do not close unknown/user processes.

Potential minimum repair: obtain explicit approval for one ordinary-user removal attempt of this exact socket entry only, then verify absence. No recursion, parent-directory cleanup, .lock/token deletion, ACL/policy change, fsutil reparsepoint delete, ownership takeover or privilege escalation. If the operation fails, stop and preserve its exact error. This is a proposed application of Microsoft's endpoint lifecycle guidance, not a tested fix.

A subsequent single Rider launch is a distinct visible operation: parent must notify user first and approval must include it. Use the recorded executable/arguments and preserve the initial launch context as closely as practical; capture process/result without silently changing runtime/profile/security options. No Steam/game or native fixture start until IDE readiness is established.

If the socket cannot be safely handled under approved ordinary permissions, stop. A support request containing the bounded logs, tag and error requires separate permission to transmit; no automatic upload. Reboot, cache/profile relocation, new runtime, software installation or security changes are not established necessary and are not proposed as automatic fallbacks.
approval_required: Any socket entry deletion/rename or other change
Any further visible program launch, after parent notification
Any additional action outside the approved ordinary-user scope
